notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2024, as the county reported them to the Census Bureau's Annual Survey of State and Local Government Finances. Not a budget.
Public schools are run by independent school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included.
Covers every fund, including water, sewer, electric and other utilities. Debt service counts interest and principal repaid; borrowing and transfers between funds are left out.
Payments to other governments ($453,000) are left out, because the government receiving them reports that spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is long-term debt outstanding plus short-term debt at year end.
Political money is not scored: contributions to Texas county candidates were not loaded.
Transparency practices have not been checked yet, so they are not scored.

Red flags: surveillance programs come from the EFF Atlas of Surveillance, a public database of news reports and public records, searched on 2026-10-18. A town or county with none listed may still have programs nobody has reported. Data center deals, corporate tax breaks and license-plate cameras mapped by volunteers have not been checked for Texas yet. Most records carry no dollar amount, so each documented program costs a quarter of the red-flag points instead of being counted as spending.

redFlags.label: License-plate readers
redFlags.detail: The Starr County Sheriff's Office has been using automated license plate readers since at least 2009.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS012182, citing ACLU

redFlags.label: Police drones
redFlags.detail: The Starr County Sheriff's Office operates one Autel Robotics Evo drone as of 2019, according to data compiled by the Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College.

source.label: EFF Atlas of Surveillance AOS003889, citing Center for the Study of the Drone at Bard College
